gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-002 identifies the same failed boundary-trace estimate in Theorem thm:added-1: the claimed gamma h^{-1} boundary contribution is O(h^{2r}), while the cut-trace and interpolation argument supports only O(h^{2r-2}). It also identifies the sharpness of the loss and supplies the corresponding corrected theorem statement.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The theorem applies the boundary trace estimate as though the gamma h^{-1} normal-trace term had the same h^{2r} rate as the volume terms, but for nonempty flux boundaries the supported and generally attainable rate is h^{2r-2}, with the lowest-order Raviart–Thomas case losing convergence altogether.

component_coverage.gold_component: The h^{2r} boundary contribution claimed for nonempty Gamma_u is unsupported; the cut-trace/interpolation calculation gives h^{2r-2}, including loss of the lowest-order Raviart–Thomas convergence guarantee.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly derives the h^{2r-2} rate from the theorem's own trace-based proof, gives a best-approximation obstruction at the same rate, and states the resulting failure of the advertised optimal-order boundary estimate.

component_coverage.gold_component: The theorem and optimal-convergence claim require a boundary-dependent correction, with the affected estimate restated at h^{2r-2}.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The proposed repair restates the theorem with volume terms at h^{2r} and the boundary term at h^{2r-2}, directly correcting the same failed estimate.
